fact.prompt: Explain in three sentences why the sky is blue.
fact.content: Sunlight contains all colors, but air molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths much more strongly than longer red ones—a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering. Because this scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every direction across the sky, we perceive the whole dome as blue. At sunset, light travels through more atmosphere, scattering the blue away and letting reds and oranges pass through to reach us directly.
